body.statement: Fix a complete label \(C\) represented in \(J\), and let \(j=(C,s)\in J\), so \(C_s=1\). Under \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\), the stratumwise holdout--stage-1 histories are independent, and each history-conditional stage-2 kernel is stratum-local and independent across retained strata. Thus, for measurable \(B_0\), \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\in B_0,E_{n,C}(\rho)\}=\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\in B_0,X_{n,s}>c_s\}\prod_{t\ne s}p_{nt}^{C_t}(1-p_{nt})^{1-C_t}\), where \(p_{nt}=\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{X_{n,t}>c_t\}\), and the same identity without \(B_0\) gives the cell probability. Under \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,\mathrm{base}}\), the product combinatorial mass on \(\prod_t\Omega_{n,1t}(\rho)\) and the stratum-local map \(X'_t\) give the same signed stage-1 factorization with \(p'_{nt}=\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,\mathrm{base}}\{X'_{n,t}>c_t\}\); after restriction to \(C'_n(\rho)=C\), the stage-2 part of \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,C}\) is an independent product over retained strata. The factorization holds likewise in \(\mathrm{def{:}gaussian\mbox{-}experiment}\). Division cancels every \(t\ne s\) signed factor under the sampling, explicit reference, and Gaussian laws, yielding exactly the displayed one-dimensional \(q_{\alpha,j}\) equation and \(\Pi_j\) integral.
body.justification: Finite-product cancellation licenses the scalar power integral for every complete signed cell over arbitrary finite \(S\).
body.gap: An active-stratum calculation alone would silently discard the other strata's positive and negative inequalities.
body.consumer: All later optimization can use the one-dimensional integral without changing the conditioning event.
body.proof_tex:
For \(t\in S\), let \(\mathcal H_{nt}\) be the holdout and stage--\(1\) assignment history in stratum \(t\).  The holdout and stage--\(1\) design assumptions make \((\mathcal H_{nt})_{t\in S}\) mutually independent.  The selector \(X_{n,t}\) and its sign event are stratum-local measurable functions of \(\mathcal H_{nt}\) and the fixed potential outcomes.  Conditional on all first-stage histories, the stage--\(2\) assumption gives mutually independent stratum-local kernels.  Equivalently, those kernels may be pregenerated and revealed only in recruited strata.  Hence, for \(j=(C,s)\), measurable \(B_0\), and \(p_{nt}=\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{X_{n,t}>c_t\}\), finite-product independence gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\in B_0,E_{n,C}(\rho)\}\\
&\quad=\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\in B_0,X_{n,s}>c_s\}
\prod_{t\in S\setminus\{s\}}p_{nt}^{C_t}(1-p_{nt})^{1-C_t}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The same identity with \(B_0\) equal to the whole space gives the cell probability.  Whenever that probability is positive, division cancels every signed factor indexed by \(t\ne s\).

Under \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,\mathrm{base}}\), the first-stage candidate mass is a finite product over \(t\in S\), and the completion and maps \(X'_{n,t}\) are stratum-local.  Thus its signed cell probability is \(\prod_{t\in S}(p'_{nt})^{C_t}(1-p'_{nt})^{1-C_t}\).  Restriction to \(C'_n=C\) divides by this product, and the subsequently generated stage--\(2\) reference law is again a product over \(\{t:C_t=1\}\).  Positivity of \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}\) licenses this division.  The same finite-product argument applies to the independent stage--\(1\) blocks and independent stage--\(2\) coordinates in the Gaussian experiment.

For the active coordinate, write
\[
X_s=a_j(\rho)h_s+Z,
\qquad
T_j=d_j(\theta_j)h_s+r_j(\rho,\theta_j)Z+v_j(\rho,\theta_j)E,
\]
with independent standard normal \(Z,E\).  At zero drift, conditioning on \(X_s>c_s\) is conditioning on \(Z>c_s\), so integrating over \(E\) gives the defining equation for \(q_{\alpha,j}\).  Under the local alternative, the condition becomes \(Z>c_s-a_j(\rho)h_s\); integrating over \(E\), then normalizing by this event's probability, gives exactly \(\Pi_j\).  All inactive-stratum positive and negative inequalities were retained until their factors canceled, and the argument used only finiteness of \(S\).
